title: Current tagged-edit baseline on durable multi-layer order cancellation
hypothesis: The expanded SQLite order fixture is solvable with the current tagged-edit harness and exercises substantial multi-file changes before any edit-tool comparison.
falsified_if: Independent correctness, scope or observed final verification fails; or successful runs remain too shallow to exercise multi-file editing. A passing baseline does not establish comparative edit-tool quality.
local_evidence: User-requested workload expansion. Original fixture at commit e65ce9d contained 7 files and 244 lines. Preserved trajectory evals/results/20260905T044831Z-multifile_order_cancellation-normal-1/trajectory.json passed with 16 tool operations and only four edit calls across three files. Version 2 adds SQLite migration, atomic inventory/payment/audit/outbox/receipt effects, durable replay, optimistic concurrency, batch commands, API/CLI and reporting. The original scenario and trace are preserved externally; version-1 outcomes must not be pooled with version 2.
deterministic_outcomes: existing regressions and public acceptance tests
external cancellation contract including concurrency and injected rollback
observed full suite after final edit
efficiency_outcomes: changed source files and changed lines
decision_rule: Seed 91802. Single-arm calibration: smoke simple_prompt and multifile_order_cancellation, then two fresh pilot repetitions of both (six total cells, three coding attempts). Freeze current source, model, reasoning, schemas, prompts, fixture and grader before calls. Maximum six launches, $12 standard-equivalent between-run cost threshold (one-run overshoot possible), 3000 active seconds; per-task timeout 900 seconds. Stop on smoke, protocol or activation failure; preserve failed attempts and register repairs as a new campaign. Offline: reference solution passes all gates, no-op fails, deliberately broken atomicity/replay/inventory/validation/reporting/CLI variants fail, protected files and final verification are enforced. Baseline-ready requires all three coding attempts to pass every gate and use the existing tagged edit interface. Workload usefulness: at least two change at least six source files and at least one uses 20+ tool operations; report duration, failure/recovery, changed lines and actual edit calls without forcing extra calls. If too shallow, expand the workload under a new fixture version. No edit-tool alternatives, default changes, speed comparison or general long-task claim in this calibration.
